section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The clipboard has been present on RISC OS for some time but is much underused. This has been addressed in RISC OS 4.2; in particular the 'standard' applications Draw, Paint and Edit have been updated with clipboard-based Cut and Paste functions in an effort to lead the initiative to see more widespread use in RISC OS.

section.title: Technical Details
section.p: To help with this, RISC OS 4.24 onwards provides two simple SWIs to provide copy and paste facilities to applications.
Data pasted onto the clipboard is stored as a typed file - much as a selection saved to the RAM disc would be.

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Type of copy to perform:
Memory copy File copy Reserved
Reserved, must be zero
Pointer to block of memory if a memory copy; pointer to filename if a file copy
Length of block of memory if a memory copy; undefined for all other uses

use.p: This call is used to copy data to the clipboard. The data must be assigned a filetype; this allows receiving applications to understand what they are dealing with. Data may be passed to the clipboard as a file or as a block of memory.
The application must, of course, implement 'cut' itself by using the SWI and then removing its own data, leaving just the copy on the clipboard.

swi-definition.name: ClipboardHolder_Paste
swi-definition.description: Request data to 'paste' from the clipboard

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Type of paste to be performed:
Paste to memory Paste to file Reserved
Only check the status and filetype Reserved, must be zero
Preferred filetype of data, or -1 to receive it in the format it was copied as
Window handle to provide clipboard data to (or 0 for a new window)

exit.register-use:
State:
Clipboard can be delivered to memory Clipboard can be delivered to file Clipboard must be delivered by the clipboard protocol Reserved, must be zero
Pointer to block of memory if a memory copy; pointer to filename if a file copy
Length of block of memory if a memory copy; preserved for file copies

use.p: This call is used to request data to paste from the clipboard. The data has been assigned a filetype when it was copied; this allows receiving applications to understand what they are dealing with.
